name: What are common mistakes in open-concept kitchen conversions?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common mistakes people make when converting a kitchen to an open-concept layout?
mainEntity.text: What are the most common mistakes people make when converting a kitchen to an open-concept layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common mistakes are surprisingly avoidable. Homeowners often focus on wall removal without planning what the new space needs to function well. That leads to poor storage, weak lighting, awkward circulation, and visible repair lines where flooring or ceilings were not fully addressed. Another common issue is assuming a wall is non-structural when it is not, which can cause delays and extra cost. Some projects also look incomplete because the cabinetry, flooring, and lighting were not designed as one system. Open-concept spaces reveal everything, so inconsistencies are easier to see. A strong plan should cover structure, storage, acoustics, finishes, appliance placement, and traffic flow before demolition starts. The goal is not just a bigger room; it is a better room that feels intentional from every angle.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common mistakes include removing the wrong wall, underestimating structural work, failing to plan storage, ignoring lighting changes, and forgetting flooring or ceiling repairs. Many open-concept projects look unfinished when design and construction are not planned together.
